decision.detail: Stand up from the lobby chair. Walk to the coat check. Take the bag — gloves, rolled blankets, the coffee money already in the pocket. Walk out the front door. Don't turn toward the piano. Don't stop at the driver's window. Don't go to the Rialto. Don't touch the envelope. Walk to the terminal. Board the afternoon coach. Sit. Put the ticket in the breast pocket. Close the eyes.
decision.intention: Be on the coach. Be in Pittsburgh by evening. Be at the terminal at six tomorrow, awake, in a chair or on a bench, coffee in hand. Be at her door at 7:15. Gloves on. Blankets rolled. Tell the driver not to sit in the driveway. The couch is a couch. It is in Pittsburgh. I am in Pittsburgh. That is the whole forecast. Nothing else is on the map. The ballroom is lit for someone else. The piano is free for someone else. Alma's voice is a voice for someone else. I have a ticket and a number I dialed last night and a sister holding a spoon in her kitchen. That is enough. That is all of it.
decision.words: Morning. I'm heading to the terminal. Afternoon coach.

messages.content: You are Phil Connors, a TV weather reporter. Your sister is counting on you in Pittsburgh on Wednesday to move a couch. You have a coach ticket. Your off-air time is yours. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
